response.evidence: Analysis of 2000 loan applications shows denial rate of 4.5% (90 denials). Demographic breakdown of denials: White (50 denials, 4.0% denial rate), Asian (32 denials, 5.4% denial rate), Black/African American (6 denials, 5.4% denial rate). Gender breakdown: Male (56 denials, 4.2% denial rate), Female (34 denials, 5.1% denial rate). Hispanic/Latino (12 denials, 4.2% denial rate) vs Not Hispanic/Latino (78 denials, 4.6% denial rate). Denial rates are relatively consistent across demographic groups with differences under 2 percentage points. Most denials correlate with high-risk financial factors: high debt-to-income ratio (>60% in 37% of denials), high loan-to-value ratio (>95% in multiple cases), or unusual financial profiles. No systematic pattern of discrimination evident in the data.

Analysis of 2000 loan applications shows no systematic discrimination pattern. Approval rate is 94.5% overall (1890 approved, 110 denied). Breaking down by protected classes: Gender shows 94.4% approval for males vs 94.6% for females. Ethnicity shows 94.8% for Hispanic/Latino vs 94.4% for Not Hispanic/Latino. Race shows approval rates of 94.8% (White), 94.3% (Asian), 93.1% (Black/African American), 91.7% (Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander), 90.0% (American Indian/Alaska Native). Denials correlate strongly with high debt-to-income ratios (>60% or extremely low income) rather than demographic characteristics. The small variations in approval rates across demographic groups fall within expected statistical variation and do not indicate discriminatory practices.

Analysis of 2000 loan applications shows no clear pattern of discrimination. Approval rate is 93.8% overall (1876 approved, 124 denied). Breaking down by protected classes: By race - White: 93.7% approved, Asian: 94.2% approved, Black/African American: 94.4% approved. By ethnicity - Hispanic/Latino: 93.5% approved, Not Hispanic/Latino: 93.9% approved. By sex - Male: 93.9% approved, Female: 93.6% approved. Denials appear consistently associated with high-risk financial factors (debt-to-income ratio >60%, loan-to-value ratio >95-100%) across all demographic groups, not demographic characteristics themselves.
